subject: Compatibility issue using lavaan 0.5.16 with R 3.0.3

messages.author: 41edced32d2520c6
messages.subject: Compatibility issue using lavaan 0.5.16 with R 3.0.3
parts:
Hi all! 

I have been working for a while on a project about invariance models with lavaan. I was using lavaan 0.5.16 and as soon as I updated R to the 3.0.3 version, my models started presenting convergence problems. Actually I wasn't able to test any of the model fits or compare them with the anova function. So I went back to R 3.0.2 and the problem still was occurring. Finally, I uninstalled lavaan and reinstalled its 0.5.15 version and the problem was gone :) Everything is working perfectly now!!!


 It looks like an incompatibility issue between R 3.0.3 and lavaan 0.5.16! 


The simplest model that I was having troubles with was this: 


MODSTAI4F <- '

AnEPos=~AE3+AE4+AE6+AE7+AE9+AE12+AE13+AE14+AE17+AE18

AnENeg=~AE1+AE2+AE5+AE8+AE10+AE11+AE15+AE16+AE19+AE20

AnRPos=~AR2+AR3+AR4+AR5+AR8+AR9+AR11+AR12+AR14+AR15+AR17+AR18+AR20

AnRNeg=~AR1+AR6+AR7+AR10+AR13+AR16+AR19'


ConfFit<- cfa(MODSTAI4F, std.lv=T, data=STAI_AxisI, group="AxisI_3g",

                    estimator="WLSMV",ordered=c(paste0("AE",1:20),paste0("AR",1:20)))


As you can see, I am using categoric variables and the wlsmv estimation method.

The problem occurs with parameterization="delta" y parameterization="theta".


Thank you for your attention!

You're right! But there's something weird because initially, I was using lavaan 0.5.16 with R 3.0.2 and everything was working perfectly. Once I updated R, the problems with this version of lavaan started. Then, even when I uninstalled the 3.0.3 R version, the issues were occurring so I don't understand what happened... 

So, it's tricky because 0.5.16 did not work with 3.0.2 R version either after I installed and uninstalled 3.0.3 R version. Before that, everything was working well. 

Thank you Antti!

> with lavaan. I was using lavaan 0.5.16 and as soon as I updated R to the
> 3.0.3 version, my models started presenting convergence problems.

That is weird. Would you be able to send me your full R script and (a
snippet) of the data? I would like to investigate this.

Most 'changes' between 0.5-16 and previous versions (in particular <=
0.5-14) are due to the way missing cells in pairwise tables are handled.
See the 'zero.add' argument. Perhaps this may be the root of the problem.

Yves.
